subject.title: Feature: a registerable, authoritative approval-resolver seam (capability-level, cross-harness, exclusive) for external approval providers

question: Should OpenClaw add a core authoritative approval-resolver contract for external providers, and if so, what capability taxonomy, resolver authority model, proof/audit contract, and cross-harness coverage are acceptable security boundaries?
rationale: This is a new security-sensitive plugin/core contract rather than a repair to an established behavior; the choice affects existing approval routes, future harnesses, and what external providers may be trusted to authorize.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped security RFC
options.body: Define the threat model and a minimal capability-level resolver contract, then implement only the paths and proof persistence that the RFC can validate.

options.title: Keep the current plugin approval model
options.body: Retain prompt-based plugin-owned approvals and document that they are not authoritative external-provider gates across all harnesses.

options.title: Defer core scope and use plugins
options.body: Direct provider authors to current trusted-policy and plugin approval APIs until a concrete missing core boundary is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped security RFC
recommendation.body: Define the threat model and a minimal capability-level resolver contract, then implement only the paths and proof persistence that the RFC can validate.

likelyOwner.reason: Their feedback on the closest prior host-API proposal indicates direct context on the intended breadth of approval extension surfaces.
